evidence.claimBoundary: 2026 Huawei production/memory mix model. Median 1.5M Ascend units, 0.88M H100e; domestic CXMT/XMC HBM supports about 240k 950DT 96GB units. Model outputs and assumptions, not provider shipment truth.
Epoch input sheet: CXMT 2026 year-end HBM exit rate 30k WSPM median (22-40k), FE yield 35% (25-45%), 8-hi backend yield 70% (55-82%), five-month lead, and XMC 3k WSPM modeled assumption.

Huawei 2026 Ascend 950 architecture whitepaper lists 950DT memory variants 144GB/96GB with 4TB/s bandwidth and 950PR 128GB/112GB with 1.6/1.4TB/s. Product specifications are vendor-owned, not independent performance validation.

Huawei rotating chairman Eric Xu says the company cannot produce enough AI computing equipment to satisfy China demand and therefore does not plan full-scale international expansion. Directional excess-demand evidence; no quantity.

Reports HBM shortage and export controls raising Chinese AI accelerator costs; Huawei 950DT indicated price >250k yuan, 20-50% above quotes two months earlier. Price is a scarcity signal, not quantity headroom.
Reports selected U.S. high-voltage transformer lead times up to 160 weeks and multi-year advance procurement. Lead time is direct schedule pressure, not a capacity/requirement ratio.

DOE identifies transformer supply-chain vulnerability; distribution-transformer lead times rose from 3-6 months in 2019 to 12-30 months in 2023 latest available on that page. Different class/time from high-voltage transformers.
Berkeley Lab reports >2,060GW generation+storage seeking U.S. transmission interconnection at end-2025. Dataset explicitly concerns generation/storage requests, not load interconnection demand.

Berkeley Lab 2026 Speed to Power documents bottlenecks slowing large-load connections and more than 40 solution classes. Establishes a load-side process problem but does not provide one national load-queue MW denominator.

ERCOT June 18 2026 says it was tracking more than 438,000MW of large-load requests, nearly 89% data centers. Requested load is not approved or energized capacity and is ERCOT-regional, not U.S.-national.

ERCOT March 2026 TAC report provides a project-status funnel for loads associated with 2026: 5,768MW observed energized, 2,759MW approved to energize but not operational, 3,181MW planning studies approved, 7,353MW under review, 2,704MW no studies submitted, total 21,765MW. This is a dated ERCOT regional project-status view, not national load demand or deliverable grid headroom.

headroomAdmission.reason: The 2,060GW Berkeley Lab figure is generation/storage interconnection while the bottleneck question is load connection and transmission deliverability. ERCOT now provides a load-side request/maturity funnel, but it remains regional and requested/qualified status is not the same as national deliverable grid capacity.
headroomAdmission.resolutionRequirement: Build region-matched funnels from requested MW → verified/studied/approved MW → contracted/energized MW → observed peak load and compare them with region-specific firm supply/transmission capability; aggregate nationally only after compatible ISO/RTO coverage exists.
